1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation. This module covers exam orientation and the course map. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What the exam is: fifty-three items, one hundred twenty minutes, a scaled score of seven hundred twenty to pass. The eight domains, their weights and the twenty-six skills behind them. The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for. The developer decision rules that explain most correct answers. How the course is built and how to use it.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Insurance
1.text: Our running case is Tidewater Insurance. Tidewater Insurance. Throughout the course you follow Tidewater Insurance, a fictional insurer. Its developers build a claims assistant: it reads claim documents, looks up policies through tools, answers adjusters and must keep customer data safe. Each module solves one problem of this application; the questions use the same style as the exam.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance
1.text: The Exam at a Glance. The figure shows this: The C C D V F exam at a glance: fifty-three items, one hundred twenty minutes, scaled score one hundred to one thousand with seven hundred twenty to pass, eight domains, U S D one hundred twenty-five, valid twelve months.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Credential or code. Claude Developer to Foundations or C C D V F. Items. fifty-three, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select. Time. one hundred twenty minutes (about two minutes fifteen seconds per item). Passing score. seven hundred twenty on a scaled range of one hundred to one thousand (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking). Fee. U S D one hundred twenty-five per attempt. Delivery. Proctored by Pearson V U E: online or at a test center. Validity. twelve months from the date the credential is awarded.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Retakes. Wait fourteen days after the first failed attempt, thirty after the second, ninety after the third; at most four attempts in a rolling twelve months; limits are per exam. Prerequisites. None are required; experience is recommended, and the credential is awarded on exam performance alone. Score report. Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail).

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Who can sit it. Exams are open to people at organizations in the Claude Partner Network who register with a company email. Others can take the free Anthropic Academy courses, which give completion certificates, not the credential. This course teaches the same knowledge to everyone. Exam tip: For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

1.text: The Eight Domains, continued. D four Eval, Testing and Debugging. Weight: two point six percent. Skills (weight): Debugging and Error Handling two point six. Modules: sixteen. Of fifty-three items, about seventeen to eighteen come from D two, nine from D five, eight from D one, six from D six, six from D eight, four from D seven, and one to two each from D three and D four. Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Each skill has a short description in the guide; items are written against it. Study order by value: D two (a third of the exam), then D five, D one, D six, D eight and D seven; D three and D four together are under six percent. Exam tip: Spend study time in proportion to the weights: the Applications and Integration domain alone is worth about as much as Agents and Prompt and Context together.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate. The minimally qualified candidate (M Q C) can. build agents and workflows with the Claude Agent S D K (software development kit) and agentic frameworks. integrate Claude through the A P I and client S D K s, including streaming and error handling. operate Claude Code and author Skills, Claude dot M D, settings.json and plugins. write effective prompts, apply context engineering, and validate output. design and run evals and debug failure modes. choose models, manage tokens, caching and batches. apply secure-by-design controls, including hooks, against prompt injection and destructive actions. build custom tools and M C P servers, and weigh built-in tools, custom tools, Skills and M C P.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued. The figure shows this: The minimally qualified candidate builds, integrates, operates, prompts, evaluates, selects models, secures and extends Claude applications.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward. Most items describe a requirement or a failure and ask for the best approach. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. one. Rule: Match the A P I to the latency need: synchronous for waiting users, batch for non-urgent bulk work. Typical wrong answers: Parallel synchronous calls to save time or money. two. Rule: Match the model to the task: the smallest model that meets the quality bar, with evals to prove it; step up when evals fail. Typical wrong answers: "Always the largest model", "always the smallest". three. Rule: Cache stable prefixes; keep volatile text after them. Typical wrong answers: Putting timestamps before the cached text.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. four. Rule: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data, keep it apart from trusted instructions, and limit what injected text can do (least privilege, hooks). Typical wrong answers: Asking the user not to attack, changing temperature, bigger model. five. Rule: Enforce hard rules in code (hooks, validation, permissions), not in prose. Typical wrong answers: Stronger prompt wording. six. Rule: Validate output: structured outputs and schemas, defensive parsing, skepticism toward confident text. Typical wrong answers: Trusting the first answer. seven. Rule: Find where the failure lives (integration layer or model output) with traces before changing prompts. Typical wrong answers: Rewriting the prompt for an H T T P error.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. eight. Rule: Keep context small and relevant: prune tool output, compact, isolate in subagents. Typical wrong answers: Sending the whole history forever. nine. Rule: Reuse through the right mechanism: M C P for shared external capabilities, Skills for procedures, custom tools for app-specific functions. Typical wrong answers: Hard-coding logic in prompts. ten. Rule: Secrets stay out of code and prompts: secrets manager, environment variables, least-privilege keys, rotation. Typical wrong answers: Keys in source or client-side code. Exam tip: When two options both work, prefer the one that is enforced, measured, least-privileged and cost-aware.

1.title: How to Use This Course
1.text: How to Use This Course. Order: read modules one to sixteen in order (they follow the domains), then module seventeen (recap) and eighteen (technique). Each module has the skills it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card. Build something. The guide recommends building and operating at least one Claude application that uses the A P I, one or more tools, basic prompt and context engineering, and simple security and evaluation practice.

1.title: How to Use This Course, continued
1.text: How to Use This Course, continued. Product details change fast. Boxes marked show current behavior (for example model I Ds, thinking modes, cache rules). On the exam, answer as the guide teaches and check the official documentation for current details. Independence. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: C C D V F; fifty-three items; one hundred twenty min; pass seven hundred twenty of one thousand; U S D one hundred twenty-five; valid twelve months. Domains: D two thirty-three point one, D five sixteen point eight, D one fourteen point seven, D six eleven point zero, D eight ten point six, D seven eight point one, D three three point one, D four two point six. Skills: twenty-six in all. Prerequisites: None required; experience recommended. Retakes: fourteen, thirty, ninety days; max four per rolling twelve months. Ten rules: Match A P I to latency, match model to task, cache stable prefixes, untrusted content stays untrusted, enforce in code, validate output, locate the failure, keep context lean, reuse through the right mechanism, secrets out of code. In the next module, we continue the course.
